answer: Each identity must finish a prescribed chain of modular squarings, with each result feeding the next. This VDF dependency prevents GPUs from splitting one evaluation to reduce its wall-clock time; a Wesolowski proof lets peers verify the result cheaply. Clones can run separate chains in parallel only with additional hardware, imposing per-identity time and resource costs—a trellis against Sybil scaling, not an absolute ban on parallel machines during the voyage to consensus by the lagoon.
